content.text:
## Review

**Clarity — Letter A.** A is built for someone reading on a phone: bolded section headers, one idea per paragraph, and a reader can skip to "A change to your advisory fee" without wading through anything else. It also translates rather than just reports — it says the index is "half global stocks, half US intermediate bonds," and it glosses the duration shortening as "we moved to bonds that mature sooner, so that money comes due closer to when you will need to withdraw it." A also closes an open loop B leaves dangling: only half the 2026 distribution has been paid, and A tells her the firm will be in touch about the rest. B leaves her to notice the gap herself.

B is four dense blocks with no headings. It opens with a sentence that carries the strategy, the net return, the fee treatment, and the gross return all at once. It uses "equities," "fixed income," "gross-of-fees," "duration," and "since inception" without unpacking any of them, and it folds the distribution figures into the middle of a paragraph about bond strategy, so two unrelated topics share one block. On a phone this is a wall.

**Tone — Letter A, but fix the salutation.** A is warm without being syrupy, and it handles the fee increase the right way: cause first, then the numbers, then an explicit invitation to call "including about the fee change." That reads as someone willing to have the conversation.

Two things go wrong in B. "We are pleased to report" is attached to a defensive duration change in a quarter that trailed its index — the cheer doesn't fit the news. And "as you navigate this important chapter of your financial life" is a florid gesture at a bereavement, from a firm writing to a woman about her late father's money. Plain English was the instruction; that line is the opposite, and it risks landing as hollow.

A's one real tone defect is the salutation. "Dear Castellanos-Weir Household" is a file label, not a greeting — B's "Dear Ines" is correct, and A should adopt it. That is a one-line edit, whereas B's problems are structural.

**Overall — Letter A.** Send A with two changes: open with "Dear Ines," and add a line giving the expected timing of the remaining $19,200 rather than the vaguer "we will be in touch."

input.reason: Clarity: A uses bolded section headers and short single-topic paragraphs suited to phone reading, and translates jargon (explains the index composition, glosses the duration shortening as bonds maturing sooner, near when she needs the money). It also flags that only half the 2026 distribution has been paid and that the firm will follow up on the rest. B is four dense blocks with no headings, opens with a sentence stacking strategy, net return, fee treatment and gross return, uses equities/fixed income/gross-of-fees/duration/since inception unglossed, and merges distribution figures into a bond-strategy paragraph. Tone: A is warm and plain, presents the fee increase cause-first and explicitly invites questions about it. B misfires twice: "We are pleased to report" attached to a defensive change in a quarter that trailed its index, and the florid "navigate this important chapter of your financial life" to a bereaved beneficiary, which cuts against the plain-English tone note. A's only tone flaw is the impersonal "Dear Castellanos-Weir Household" where B correctly uses "Dear Ines" — a one-line fix against B's structural problems. Length was not a factor; the letters are comparable in size and A wins on organization, not volume.
